name: TT (Family) Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Parent, spouse, or child of a Vietnamese citizen; or spouse or minor child (under 18) of a foreigner holding specified visa categories (e.g. LV, DT, LS, NN1, DH, TT, LD).
A notarized sponsorship commitment from the Vietnamese-citizen or resident-foreigner sponsor, plus notarized marriage/birth certificates proving the family tie.

evidence_required.document: Notarized marriage or birth certificate proving the family tie
Sponsorship commitment letter from the Vietnamese-citizen or resident-foreigner sponsor

outcome.duration_length: visa up to 1 year; temporary residence card up to 3 years, renewable

sources.title: LuatVietnam (private legal database) -- consolidated Law on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence of Foreigners: TT family visa category, up to 1 year, Article 9
EIV (education consultancy) -- Vietnam Temporary Residence Card guide: TT-based residence card up to 3 years, sponsorship and notarized-document requirements for family members of Vietnamese citizens

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Vietnam). STATUS: DRAFT, TIER-3 ONLY -- no genuine .gov.vn source with TT-specific procedural detail was found in this pass. work_rights is 'none': a TT holder is not automatically authorized to work and would need a separate work permit or exemption, not modeled as automatic here. citizenship_after_months (0) and dual_citizenship_allowed (true) point to vn_citizenship_relaxed_naturalisation.json's July-2025-amended track for spouses/children of Vietnamese citizens, which waives the standard 5-year residence, language, and financial-means tests entirely -- see that file's notes for the live-legal-change caveat. leads_to_pr (true, 36 months) reflects the 'family member of a Vietnamese citizen already holding permanent residence' category in vn_permanent_residence.json -- but note that file requires the SPONSOR to hold permanent residence specifically, which a Vietnamese citizen by definition does not need (citizens aren't 'permanent residents' of their own country) -- this creates a genuine ambiguity in how a plain Vietnamese-citizen spouse's dependent would qualify for thường trú under the family category, which the tier-1 source did not resolve; disclosed as an open question rather than resolved by assumption.
